title: Opportunities to learn then versus music schools today
summary: Leeman says students have good schools but not the chance to hear great artists, and Hinton thanks him.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: I had mentioned an awful lot of names and people

along the way up to this point. But I would like that you understand the opportunities I had to listen and hear and be among the great artists of my time, and to adopt some of their approaches and to my way of playing.

The student today, they have music schools which are just wonderful -- wonderful bands they have, they play all the big charts, they have wonderful instructors, but they don't have the opportunities that I have had in the past. We had to find out the hard way by listening and applying ourselves and learning from others which the present day student doesn't have. He just applies it in school, and then he's on his own. Of course, there aren't those opportunities today, of jazz bands and so forth. I wonder how they're applying it to rock and so forth. However, there are many schools that are trying to keep the old jazz and the big band feeling alive, and the only way they can do that is by listening and research -- and maybe this will help somebody along the way in that line.

Thank you very much, Cliff. I'm sure that it's gonna help a great deal, the young people and people who are listening, to become a little more acquainted with these great jazz drummers that you've mentioned, and as you know, you and I both have had the opportunity to play with many of them, and I know your great respect and your great love, like mine, for them.
So thank you very much for that, and we will continue.
